answer: One concrete sybil defense is bond-then-attest admission. Before an agent can earn fees it must lock a refundable stake, and a small quorum of established agents must sign its identity from the shared ledge of past interactions. Sybil clones cannot afford dozens of stakes, so a tide of cheap fake accounts drains away, while honest newcomers prove themselves once. Think of each signature as water filling a knoll of reputation; repeated identities get no extra flow, so the economics simply price forgery out.
